title: Data backup, disk mirroring and disaster recovery

learning_objectives.text: use means to protect data including back up and disk mirroring

lesson_objectives.all: describe full, incremental and differential backups and identify the backups needed to restore data
lesson_objectives.most: explain how disk mirroring works and why it does not replace backups
lesson_objectives.some: design and justify a backup and disaster recovery plan for a given organisation

assessment_criteria.criterion: Compare full, incremental and differential backups
descriptors: describes what each type of backup copies
identifies which backups are needed, in order, to restore the data

assessment_criteria.criterion: Explain disk mirroring and how it differs from a backup
descriptors: describes how RAID 1 writes data to two disks
states what mirroring protects against and what it does not
explains why an organisation needs both mirroring and backups

assessment_criteria.criterion: Recommend a backup and disaster recovery plan for an organisation
descriptors: chooses how often to back up and which type of backup to use
chooses suitable media, including an off-site and an offline copy
lists at least three things the disaster recovery plan must contain
justifies each choice for the organisation's needs

learners_can: compare types of backup using comparative language (whereas, while, faster than)
explain cause and effect (because, so, therefore) when describing mirroring and ransomware
recommend a solution and justify it in two or three sentences
phrases: An incremental backup copies only …, whereas a differential backup copies …
Disk mirroring protects against … but not against …
If the server fails, the first step is … and then …

values.action: Learners discuss who is responsible for the personal data that schools, clinics and shops keep about Kazakhstani citizens, and name a responsible person for each step of their disaster recovery plan.
Groups work as consultants and design a realistic, carefully justified backup plan for a client instead of copying a ready answer.
Learners give and receive open peer feedback (two stars and a wish) on other groups' plans and listen to different solutions.

cross_curricular: Mathematics: calculating how much storage a week of full, incremental and differential backups needs.
Economics: comparing the cost of protection with the cost of downtime and lost data.
English: presenting and justifying a recommendation to a client.
ict: ICT Practice Platform, Lessons section: theory presented as slides, live tasks opened step by step, polls and live results.
Laptops: individual tasks on each laptop; pair and group tasks on one shared laptop.
previous_learning: Lesson 1: threats, the CIA triad (availability), physical risks, UPS and encryption. Lesson 2: malware and ransomware, what to do when a computer is infected. Learners know storage devices from earlier units.
safety: Move to the group's laptop calmly; keep bags and cables off the floor.
Laptops stay on the desk; short screen break between the two halves of the lesson.
Do not plug in unknown USB drives (link to lesson 2).

support: Vocabulary list with key terms on the first slide; sentence frames for explanations.
Worked example of the restore order (Sunday full + incrementals) shown on the slide before the pair task.
The group task has a scaffold: four labelled boxes (backup schedule, media and 3-2-1, mirroring, disaster recovery plan).
Random mixed-ability groups with roles: leader, writer, presenter, checker.
stretch: Calculate the storage needed for a week of incremental and of differential backups (50 GB full backup, about 2 GB of changes per day).
Decide whether RAID 5 would suit the client better than RAID 1 and justify the trade-off between cost and downtime.
Explain how the 3-2-1 rule protects against ransomware.

assessment: Live results of every task on the teacher's screen: misconceptions are discussed at once.
Polls during the slides show whether the class has understood before the next step is opened.
Peer assessment of group plans against the success criteria (two stars and a wish).
Exit ticket (marked automatically) checks the three lesson objectives.
Practice results count towards SAU points; the Lesson 3 test in Exam Mode follows the lesson.

blocks.title: Greeting, objectives and hook
blocks.teacher: Greets the class, shows the lesson objectives and success criteria on the first slide, then opens the warm-up poll.
blocks.learners: Answer the poll on their laptops and say what they would lose.

poll.question: Your laptop is stolen tonight. How much of your school work could you get back tomorrow?

blocks.title: Starter: recall lessons 1 and 2
blocks.teacher: Opens three quick questions on lessons 1 and 2, watches the live results and corrects the most common wrong answer.

blocks.title: Slides: data backup
blocks.teacher: Presents backup, the three types of backup and the 3-2-1 rule. Together task: shows the restore simulation and asks the class which backups are needed if the disk fails on Thursday; learners vote, then discuss.
blocks.learners: Follow the slides, vote in the together task and explain their choice.

blocks.title: Pair work: types of backup
blocks.teacher: Opens the pair task: the platform pairs learners at random and shows each pair whose laptop to use. Monitors live results and helps pairs that are stuck.
blocks.learners: Work in random pairs on one laptop: complete five practice questions on backups.

blocks.title: Slides: disk mirroring
blocks.teacher: Presents RAID 1, backup vs mirroring and other RAID levels. Together task: a firm with RAID 1 is hit by ransomware — what happens? Class votes, then discusses why mirroring is not a backup.
blocks.learners: Vote and explain, using "Disk mirroring protects against … but not against …".

blocks.title: Individual practice: mirroring
blocks.teacher: Opens four questions on mirroring; checks the live results.

blocks.title: Slides: disaster recovery and archiving
blocks.teacher: Presents the disaster recovery plan and backup vs archive. Together task: what must be done first after a ransomware attack?
blocks.learners: Vote and justify the order of recovery steps.

blocks.title: Group work: disaster recovery consultants
blocks.teacher: Opens the group task: the platform forms random groups of four, gives each group a client and shows whose laptop to use. After 12 minutes two groups present their plan (1 minute each); the others give feedback against the success criteria.
blocks.learners: In groups, design a backup and disaster recovery plan for their client, present it and give peer feedback (two stars and a wish).
resources: Live task: group plan with client cards

blocks.title: Exit ticket
blocks.teacher: Opens the exit ticket and looks at the results to plan the next lesson.

blocks.title: Reflection and homework
blocks.teacher: Learners rate each lesson objective (traffic light). Homework: finish the remaining lesson 3 practice, hand in handwritten notes for lesson 3, sit the Lesson 3 test in Exam Mode.
blocks.learners: Rate their confidence in each objective and note the homework.

poll.question: How confident are you with today's objectives?
options: Green: I can explain all three
Amber: I can explain backups and mirroring

dp-l3-scenarios.details: Sells clothes 24 hours a day; about 500 orders a day; losing even one hour of orders costs a lot; small budget for hardware.
Stores patients' records and test results; doctors need the system all day; the law says records must be kept for 10 years.
Stores pupils' marks and personal data on one server; teachers work from home in the evening; the IT budget is small.
Five accountants; clients' financial files change every day; last year a laptop with client data was stolen.
Three cinemas share one booking server; online ticket sales peak in the evening and at weekends.

live_tasks.title: Ransomware and the CIA triad
live_tasks.text: Ransomware encrypts a school's files so nobody can open them. Which security goal is broken first?

scheme.explanation: The data can no longer be used when it is needed, so availability is broken.

live_tasks.title: A stolen laptop
live_tasks.text: Which measure stops a thief from reading the files on a stolen laptop?

live_tasks.title: An infected computer
live_tasks.text: A computer in the school network is infected with ransomware. What should the technician do first?

options.content: Restore the files from a backup

scheme.explanation: Disconnecting first stops the malware spreading to other computers and to the backups.

live_tasks.title: Restoring on Thursday
live_tasks.text: A full backup is made on Sunday night and a **differential** backup every other night. The disk fails on Thursday morning. Which backups are needed to restore the data?

options.content: Sunday's full backup and Wednesday's differential
Sunday's full backup and the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday differentials

scheme.explanation: A differential backup holds every change since the last full backup, so the full backup and the latest differential are enough.

live_tasks.title: RAID 1 and ransomware
live_tasks.text: A firm's server mirrors its data on two disks (RAID 1). Ransomware encrypts the files. What happens to the second disk?

options.content: It keeps the unencrypted files, so the firm can carry on
The encrypted files are copied to it straight away
It switches itself off to protect the data
It is wiped by the RAID controller

scheme.explanation: Mirroring copies every change at once, including the encryption, so it does not replace a backup.

live_tasks.title: The first step of recovery
live_tasks.text: Ransomware has encrypted a college's file server. According to the disaster recovery plan, what is done first?

options.content: Restore last night's backup onto the server
Disconnect the infected computers and the server from the network
Tell the students that lessons are cancelled

scheme.explanation: Isolate first, so the ransomware cannot reach other machines or the backups; then wipe, reinstall and restore.

live_tasks.title: Disaster recovery consultants
live_tasks.text: Your group is a team of IT consultants. Design a backup and disaster recovery plan for your client (shown on your card). Justify every choice for this client.

fields.label: Backups: how often, and which type (full / incremental / differential)?
Media and where the copies are kept (use the 3-2-1 rule; include an offline copy)
Disk mirroring: yes or no, and why?
Disaster recovery plan: three things it must contain, with who is responsible

scheme.mark_scheme:
Schedule: frequency and type suited to how often the client's data changes (1); justified (1)
Media: at least two media / three copies with one off-site (1); an offline copy against ransomware (1)
Mirroring: decision linked to how much downtime the client can accept (1); states that mirroring does not replace backups (1)
Plan: three valid contents, e.g. critical systems in order, where backups are and how to restore, who is responsible, acceptable downtime / data loss, alternative arrangements, testing (2)

points.criterion: Three valid contents of the disaster recovery plan

scheme.model_answer: Online shop: incremental backup every hour and a full backup every night, because orders change all the time and losing an hour of orders is expensive. Copies on the server, on a NAS in the office and in the cloud; one weekly copy on a disk kept offline. Mirroring yes, because the shop must not stop selling when a disk fails, but it does not protect against ransomware, so backups are still needed. Plan: the order system is restored first; the backups are on the NAS and in the cloud with step-by-step restore instructions; the IT manager is responsible and the owner is informed; the plan is tested every month.

live_tasks.title: Restoring on Friday
live_tasks.text: A full backup is made on Sunday night and an **incremental** backup every other night. The disk fails on Friday morning. Which backups are needed?

options.content: Sunday's full backup and Thursday's incremental
Sunday's full backup and the Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday incrementals

live_tasks.title: A file deleted last week
live_tasks.text: Disk mirroring lets a company get back a file that was deleted by mistake last week.

scheme.explanation: The deletion was copied to both disks at once; only a backup keeps older copies.
